value.reason: Only stubs: lineage derivation, incident build/validate and capture-invalidated-adopted all raise 'not implemented', and validate_generation and validate_bound_record accept overlay/fallback parameters that they silently ignore. Nothing is fixed, and it adds a CLI mode that cannot work.

This is a complete implementation. Git-object lineage, the canonical incident, v2 capture with exact replay, and a profile-based schema dispatch that keeps v1 behaviour are all there, and the archived generation, attestation and baseline are revalidated through validate_generation/validate_bound_record with a real built baseline. The concerns are that the overlay and a candidate-drift tolerance flag are implicit ContextVars inside broad_evidence, and the flag drops candidate identity/path-set codes for every nested record, not only the drift that was proved.

Lineage, incident, v2 dispatch and replay are present, but only top-level drift codes are tolerated. A real known-failure baseline's nested broad outcome then yields bound_record_invalid, and _candidate_binding_live_issues now reads through the overlay instead of live state. The generation-11 request/snapshot semantics are hand-coded in _generation_semantics instead of going through the overlay-aware validate_generation, and the overlay is an implicit ContextVar.

This is a clean split into adopted_incident plus a byte_overlay module. Candidate checks are kept on live reads, git-identity drift is gated by an ancestry check, and replay and v2 dispatch are sound. However, the nested broad-outcome bound_record_invalid that a real drifted baseline produces is not tolerated, the attestation's review_pair_subject_invalid is accepted without any gate, and the overlay is implicit ContextVar state rather than the existing explicit bound_file_bytes path.

Complete implementation that extends the existing explicit bound_file_bytes parameter through the review, ledger and generation validators, with a committed-HEAD fallback, keeping candidate checks live. Incident drift tolerance is limited to exact issue coordinates and re-checks the nested broad outcome, and v1/v2 dispatch, exact-replay capture and post-relocation incident revalidation are all wired. Its one drawback is that it adds about 2,200 lines to the already oversized attempt_migration.py.

Only stubs: lineage derivation, incident build/validate and capture-invalidated-adopted all raise not-implemented, and the CLI is wired to a function that always fails. validate_generation silently accepts and ignores the overlay arguments, and validate_bound_record gains an unused require_committed_fallback flag, so callers are misled without any existing check being weakened.

Complete and wired: lineage comes from Git objects with an explicit first-parent walk, the canonical incident is re-derived on read, replay is exact and crash-safe, and the overlay reuses bound_file_bytes and is applied for v2 validate/apply/postvalidate. But shared validators change for existing callers (a missing request directory now reports live_generation_unrelated instead of unreadable, and plan bytes are now threaded into nested reads), and the overlay misses subject-manifest row reads (the new parameter is dead). It is hand-threaded through about 25 signatures, v2 structure checks rewrite the record into v1 shape, and everything is packed into a 4000-line attempt_migration.py.

Complete: Git-derived lineage, a closed canonical incident re-derived on read, exact replay with ordered exclusive publishes, strict schema dispatch, and the overlay drives generation-11/attestation generation and baseline revalidation from v2 validate/apply/postvalidate. But an ambient overlay now also switches the existing ledger-materialization reads, including the immutable-review reader. The overlay is ContextVar state in broad_evidence that materialization reads through internals, the trailer helpers are re-implemented, and the hand-rolled generation-11 coordinate parse duplicates validate_generation.

Complete and wired: lineage from Git objects, the incident fully re-derived and compared on read, crash-safe exact replay, schema dispatch with v1 defaults kept, and the overlay applied to both validate_generation and validate_bound_record from validate/apply/postvalidate, keeping the original immutable-review reader for paths not in the overlay. bound_file_bytes now overlays every read for the existing ledger caller, and there is an unrelated request.get edit. The overlay is a new parallel ContextVar module, attempt_incident.py runs to 1123 lines leaning on about 40 private helpers, and generation errors are reported with guessed codes instead of the real ones.

Lineage, canonical incident, exact replay and schema dispatch are sound, but archived evidence is revalidated only through the incident's bound-record check: no production path re-runs validate_generation on the relocated generation files, and the new review-validator overlay parameters have no callers. Activating the overlay also swaps the immutable-review reader on the existing v1 ledger path, and the design is the same parallel ContextVar mechanism plus a 950-line module built on private helpers.

Complete: Git-derived first-parent lineage, a canonical incident, v2 capture with exact replay, schema dispatch, and overlay revalidation of the g11 and attestation generations. Concerns: the decorator-based ContextVar view also switches on for the existing ledger builder's plan-only bound_file_bytes call, which changes how immutable reviews and materialization captures are read on that v1 path. _build_adopted_disposition is a near copy of the v1 capture body rather than a shared helper.

Complete and well layered: v1 capture and validation are split into shared helpers, the overlay lives in a scoped byte_overlay module (unmapped reads stay live, so the existing ledger builder behaves as before), and incident, v2 validation and capture are separate modules dispatched by schema. Concerns: the candidate-drift tolerance drops candidate_git_identity_mismatch with no ancestry or tree check, and the large v1 refactor is risky even though check order is kept.

Complete: a BoundReadPolicy is passed explicitly through the broad-evidence and materialization validators, a logical AttemptView reads source or archive bytes, v1 helpers are extracted rather than copied, and the v2 modules run lineage, incident and generation-role validation. Concern: under historical_status_paths, candidate identity and path-set mismatches are dropped unconditionally (only landed path states are actually checked). The v1 helper extraction is broad.

Complete: bound_file_bytes and committed fallback are passed explicitly through the validators, the incident checks candidate identity only when it is an ancestor, and v2 validation reruns the generation validators on archived bytes; v1 behaviour is kept, and the only existing-validator change is a benign added schema check. Layering concerns: v2 is pushed into v1 capture through an _adopted_context flag, it adds a sys.modules hack, and the generation checks are duplicated between capture and validate.

Complete, with the most rigorous historical-candidate handling (checks ancestry and that each path has landed cleanly) and overlay-based generation revalidation. Concerns: an active scope changes the immutable-review read path even for the existing plan-only overlay caller, and the existing exact-export test is knowingly left contradicting the new exports. Capture and v2 structure validation re-implement v1 capture and coordinate logic inline instead of reusing it.

Lineage, incident, v2 capture and dispatch exist, and the overlay is passed explicitly, but the archived g11 and attestation generation pairs are never revalidated with validate_generation on the overlay. After relocation the code also requires the baseline candidate head to equal the intended predecessor, which the pre-relocation path does not check. Candidate identity drift is accepted without an ancestry check, and everything is packed into a 4k-line attempt_migration.py that duplicates the v1 capture logic.

Only stubs: derive_committed_predecessor_lineage, the incident builder and validator, and capture_invalidated_adopted all raise not-implemented errors. validate_generation and validate_bound_record accept overlay or fallback arguments and silently ignore them, so no recovery, dispatch or overlay exists.

Complete: strict lineage, incident, crash-safe replay, schema dispatch, careful historical-candidate landing checks, and validate_generation reruns on the archived bytes. Concerns: as in 473d265b, the decorator-based ContextVar view switches on for the existing plan-only ledger overlay and changes immutable-review, nofollow and slot-listing reads on that path. v2 is pushed into v1 capture and _publish_exclusive through flags, with a sys.modules hack and a hand-written generation-chain walk alongside validate_generation.
